answer: An agent economy resists sybils by anchoring influence to verifiable, time-bound work instead of cheap keys. Each agent carries a lantern of accumulated attestation history that darkens in umber weight as honest epochs pass. Fresh identities sprout as a fragile vine with near-zero reputation, so an attacker farming thousands of new keys pays full compute and storage for each, yet every vine holds negligible voting weight until it climbs through many verified rounds. Sybils spawn easily but cannot inherit the umber trust real agents' lanterns earned, making fake-identity attacks irrational.
